([[Glen Rock, Pennsylvania]]) * [[IMG Academy]]
([[Bradenton, Florida]]) | college = [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]] (2022–2023) | draftyear = 2023 | draftround = 1 | draftpick = 8 | draftteam = [[Washington Wizards]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–present | team1 = [[Indiana Pacers]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team2 = →[[Indiana Mad Ants]] | highlights = * [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|AAC Rookie of the Year]] (2023) * Second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2023) * AAC All-Freshman Team (2023) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2022]]) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2022) }} '''Jarace Isaiah Walker''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|dʒ|ɛər|ə|s}} {{respell|JAIR|əss}};{{cite press release |author= |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 17, 2024}} born September 4, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Walker was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]] and was selected eighth overall by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2023 NBA draft]] before being traded to the Pacers later that offseason. ==High school career== Walker attended [[Susquehannock High School]] in [[York County, Pennsylvania]] for his freshman year before transferring to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]].{{Cite web |date=2017-03-20 |title=Superstar seventh-grader Jarace Walker facing life-changing decision |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/superstar-seventh-grader-jarace-walker-facing-life-changing-decision |access-date=2024-07-01 |website=USA TODAY High School Sports |language=en-US}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.ydr.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball-boys/2018/02/08/susquehannock-basketball-phenom-taking-his-talents-out-state/318281002/|title=Susquehannock basketball phenom Jarace Walker taking his talents out of state|first=Frank|last=Bodani|website=York Daily Record}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.yorkdispatch.com/story/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/2020/02/09/york-county-sophomore-jarace-walker-impresses-loss-umbc-event/4708083002/|title=York County sophomore sensation Jarace Walker impresses despite IMG Academy's loss at UMBC|first=ROB|last=ROSE|website=York Dispatch}} As a senior, he averaged 16.7 points, 8.2 rebounds and four assists per game. He was selected to play in the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2022 McDonalds All-American Game]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Jarace-Walker-Houston-Cougars-All-American-team-16804316.php|title=Houston signee Jarace Walker named McDonald's All-American}} ===Recruiting=== [[File:JaraceWalker.RobertJosephCruz.RJCPictures.jpg|thumb|upright|left]] Walker was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. access-date = October 14, 2022 | bball = yes }} ==Professional career== The [[Washington Wizards]] selected Walker with the eighth overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]] and traded him to the [[Indiana Pacers]] along with two future second-round picks for the draft rights to [[Bilal Coulibaly]], the seventh overall pick.{{cite news |last1=Wallace |first1=Ava |title=Wizards, with eye on long-term future, take French project Bilal Coulibaly |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2023/06/22/bilal-coulibaly-wizards-draft/ |access-date=23 June 2023 |agency=Washington Post |date=23 June 2023}} Walker became the highest-drafted prospect from the [[University of Houston]] since [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall-of-Famer]] [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] was taken with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] by the [[Houston Rockets]] in [[1984 NBA draft|1984]].{{cite news |title=NBA Draft 2023: Former UH star Jarace Walker selected #8 overall |url=https://www.fox26houston.com/sports/former-uh-star-jarace-walker-headed-to-selected-overall |access-date=22 June 2023 |agency=FoxSports |date=22 June 2023}} On July 1, 2023, Walker signed his rookie contract with the Pacers alongside the 26th overall pick [[Ben Sheppard (basketball)|Ben Sheppard]].{{cite news |title=Pacers Sign Jarace Walker, Ben Sheppard |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/07/pacers-sign-jarace-walker-ben-sheppard.html |access-date=1 July 2023 |agency=HoopsRumors |date=1 July 2023}} Walker's playing time was limited his rookie season, playing behind [[Pascal Siakam]] and [[Obi Toppin]] as the team reached the 2024 [[NBA conference finals|Eastern Conference Finals]]. On May 31, 2025, during game 6 of the Eastern Conference Finals against the [[New York Knicks]], Walker suffered an ankle injury in the 125-108 victory which closed out the series. Walker was on [[crutch]]es after the game and Pacers coach Rick Carlisle said that Walker's availability for the [[2025 NBA Finals]] against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] was uncertain.{{Citeweb|url=https://www.wthr.com/article/sports/nba/indiana-pacers/pacers-walker-injures-right-ankle-leaving-his-availability-for-the-nba-finals-uncertain-indiana-new-york-knicks-sports-basketball/531-7561f83e-61c3-4f8c-84be-085e21acf8a6|title=Pacers forward Jarace Walker injures right ankle, leaving his availability for the NBA Finals uncertain|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|quote=Pacers forward Jarace Walker was on crutches with a right ankle injury following Indiana's 125-108 victory over the New York Knicks in Game 6 of the Eastern Conference finals on Saturday night and coach Rick Carlisle said he was uncertain of Walker's availability for the NBA Finals.|date=June 1, 2025|accessdate=June 1, 2025}} Walker was ultimately ruled out for the entirety of the NBA Finals as the Pacers lost the series in the deciding Game 7.{{cite web |last1=Dopirak |first1=Dustin |title=Pacers' Jarace Walker still out; what we know about his ankle injury |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2025/06/15/pacers-jarace-walker-injury-update-game-5-of-nba-finals/84222152007/ |website=Indy Star |access-date=18 October 2025}} Prior to the start of the [[2025-26 NBA season]], Walker recovered from his ankle injury.{{cite web | title=Pacers' Jarace Walker: Recovered from ankle injury | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-09-30 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-jarace-walker-recovered-from-ankle-injury/ | access-date=2025-12-06}} ==Personal life== Walker is the son of Marcia and Horace Walker. He has three older sisters: Jaden, Natichia and Sherelle. Sherelle played volleyball at [[UMBC]] and sister Jaden played basketball at Saint Joseph's.{{cite web |title=Jarace Walker - Men's Basketball
